sentences.text:
On the occasion of marriage, on 01.05.2014, all the household articles including bed, TV,
utensils, clothes, fridge, etc. and gold and silver ornaments were also given.
In all, her parents had spent about Rs.30 lakh in marriage.

When respondent No.2 went to her matrimonial home for the first time after the marriage, she found that applicants were discussing about the goods and cash given in marriage and saying that it was decided to spend Rs.60-70 lakh in marriage, but her father has performed the entire marriage in about Rs.30 lakhs only.
Then, all the applicants called her and pressurized to bring additional Rs.40 lakh cash in dowry from her father.

Since she did not thought it appropriate to say anything to her in-laws on her first visit to matrimonial home, therefore, she told them that when she would go to her parents' house, then she would tell her father and make him talk with them.

After respondent No.2 went to her parental home, she informed her father and brothers that her in-laws have demanded Rs.40 lacs in dowry on the ground that the entire marriage was not performed in Rs.70 lacs.

On this, her father talked to her mother-in-law, father-in-law and husband and informed them that he had performed the marriage in accordance with the pre-marital discussions done with them and that he is not financially capable to fulfill their demand.

On this,
they threatened that if her father cannot fulfill the demand then he should keep respondent No.2 with him.

Thereafter, her family members, somehow at social level, convinced her in-laws to take her back and then her husband took and left her with his parents at Village Kheriya, while he himself started residing at the place of his posting i.e. Dabra.
During holidays, he used to come to his native Village and harass respondent No.2 for non fulfillment of demand of dowry.

Her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10184 father-in-law, mother-in-law, sister-in-law and her husband also used to support him and assault her and deprive her of food, proper clothing etc.
and say that so long as her parents do not fulfill their demand, she would be treated like this only and will have to live like a servant in the Village.
Her husband never took her to any of the places of his postings.
On her request to keep her with him, her husband used to abuse, assault and physically torture her and tell his parents and brother-in-law to take as much work as possible from her.
Respondent No.2 was tolerating all this under the hope and belief that things would improve some day, but the conduct of her in-laws did not improve.
During her stay in matrimonial home, even while she was pregnant, no arrangement was made for her proper food and treatment by her husband, mother-in-law and father-in-law.

When she informed her parents, then her parents urged her in-laws through their relatives, to keep her properly and apprised them they are not in a position to fulfill the demand of Rs.40 lacs as they have already spent around Rs.12 lacs for kidney transplantation of their son Indrapal, but the applicants were adamant.

It is alleged that respondent No.2 remained in the matrimonial house for a very short period and during this period when she got pregnant about 2 years back, she was turned out of the house in the clothes worn by her and applicants told her that unless she brings Rs. 40 lacs, they would not allow her to stay in the matrimonial house.
Then she informed her father and brother, who brought her back to Gwalior.

It is further alleged that previously also, on 1/9/2014, respondent No.2 had given a written complaint at Mahila Thana, Padav against the applicants, on which, after reconciliation proceedings done by Police Thana Padav, she was sent with her husband.
Her husband took her and left her with his parents in Village.

During reconciliation proceedings, applicants had assured her father and brother that they would keep her properly and would not harass her on account of non fulfillment of demand of dowry, but after some time, her husband brought her NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10184 from Village Kheria on the pretext of medical check-up, but did not get her Rajeev Kumar Purohit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83901117/
2 medically examined and instead left her outside her house and did not return.

When her father talked with her husband, he informed her father that unless he fulfills their demand of dowry, he would not keep respondent No.2 with him.
It is alleged that for the last two years her husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law have never tried to contact her, nor given any maintenance etc.
On saying anything, they threaten that they will get their son married somewhere else to get more money and it is not possible to keep her.
It is alleged that the in-laws of respondent No.2 are greedy for dowry and they have also kept her entire Stridhan.
It is also alleged that they also threaten her with life.
Accordingly, FIR was lodged against the present applicants.

4. It was submitted by counsel for applicants that parties have amicably settled the dispute and accordingly this Court, by order dated 23.04.2025, had directed the parties to appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court for verification of factum of compromise.
5.

The Principal Registrar, after recording statements of parties, has submitted the following report:
01.05.2025
In compliance of Hon'ble Court order dated 23.04.2025 the matter is placed before me for verification of compromise.

Complainant/Respondent No.2 Smt Laxmi @ Parwati Purohit is present alongwith his Counsel Ms.
Pratika Pathak Adv who has identified them.

Accused/Applicant No.1 Rajeev Kumar Purohit, No.2 Ramdatt Sharma, No.3 Smt Munni Devi, No.4 Mukesh Kumar Bhatele and No.5 Smt Arti NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10184 Sharma are present alongwith their counsel Shri Rishi Kumar Katare Adv who has identified them.
Name of Accused/Applicant No.1, 3 and 4 are different in Aadhar Card and F.I.R. and Surname of Accused/Applicant No.2,5 and Complainant are different in Aadhar Card and F.I.R.
However they submits that they have filed affidavit in support of compromise application wherein their correct Name/surname mentioned.
Parties have submitted copy of their Aadhar Cards regarding their identification.
Parties have filed I.A. No. 27217/2024 and I.A. No. 27218/2024 for compromise alongwith their affidavit.
Statements of Complainant/Respondent and Accused/applicants are recorded.

Matter perused,
inquired and verified as to factum of compromise.

Having verified the factum of compromise from the Complainant/Respondent and Accused/Applicants, I am of the view that rival parties have arrived at compromise voluntarily,
without any threat, inducement or coercion.
Report is submitted accordingly.

6. Thus, it is clear that parties have amicably settled their dispute.

Since it is a family dispute and the allegations are not against the society, therefore FIR in Crime No.101/2018 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Gwalior (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506, 34 of IPC and S.4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and criminal prosecution arising out of the same are quashed on the basis of compromise.
Applicants are acquitted.
7. Application succeeds and is hereby allowed.
